findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without cacheMu, and this PR adds a startup caller
findings.body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`, while `BuildIndex` writes to the same map under `cacheMu.Lock()`. The PR now calls `s.search.TotalDocs()` from `searchSupport.init` for the new log line. That call runs right after the goroutine consuming `WatchWriteEvents` is started, and that goroutine calls `handleEvent`, then `getOrCreateIndex`, then `BuildIndex`, which writes to the map. The first event for a resource that was skipped by `InitMinCount` therefore races with the unlocked read. Go can abort the process with 'fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write'. `TotalDocs` should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds, and the overwritten index is never closed
findings.body: The old whole-function lock serialized builds, and it also made `GetIndex` (which takes `RLock`) block until a build finished. With the lock removed, `GetIndex` returns nil while a build is in flight. Two concurrent callers of `getOrCreateIndex` for the same key (for example two searches, or a search plus a watch event, for a resource under `InitMinCount`) then both run a full `BuildIndex`. The work is duplicated and `IndexTenants` is incremented twice. For file-backed indexes the second `bleve.New(dir)` fails on the existing directory. For in-memory indexes the second build silently replaces the first in `b.cache` without closing it, which leaks the old bleve index. `BuildIndex` needs per-key de-duplication (singleflight or a per-key lock), or at least a re-check and close of any existing cache entry when inserting.

findings.title: Stop() sets initErr but nothing reads it any more, so requests are no longer rejected during shutdown
findings.body: Every handler used to call `s.Init(ctx)`, which returned `s.initErr`. `Stop` set `initErr` to 'service is stopping' or 'service is stopped', so requests arriving during or after shutdown failed fast. This PR removes all of those calls and `Init` is now only called from the constructor. `Stop` still writes `initErr`, but nothing consumes it. Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch and the rest now run against a stopped backend or a closed DB and fail with confusing errors. There is also an unsynchronized write to `initErr`. A cheap stopped-state check should be restored in the handlers, or the dead state removed.

findings.title: Failed Init in the constructor leaves the context, lifecycle and backend resources un-cleaned
findings.body: When `s.Init(ctx)` fails in `NewResourceServer`, the function returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()` and without calling `lifecycle.Stop`. Init may already have run the lifecycle `Init` (opening the DB), run the search `init` (which starts an event-consuming goroutine on `context.Background()`), or started the broadcaster, so those leak. Because Init is now eager in the constructor, this error path is reachable at startup. `cancel` (and ideally the lifecycle Stop) should be invoked before returning the error. `Init` also already logs the same error, so it is logged twice.

findings.title: Test is skipped for postgres instead of fixing a likely regression from eager init
findings.body: The PR adds a skip with 'test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally' to the only test that exercises the storage-server module. That test now starts the resource server through `InitializeModuleServer`, which runs the eagerly-initialized resource server. A failure appearing in CI right after moving initialization into the constructor suggests the change breaks something in that startup path (for example the DB or lifecycle init order, or timing). Skipping hides this, and postgres coverage for the module server is lost. The root cause should be investigated, or at least tracked in an issue rather than a bare TODO.

findings.title: Trace-context propagation fix is incomplete: other spans still discard the derived context
findings.body: The PR is described as fixing trace propagation, but only `GetResourceStats` was changed to `ctx, span := ...`. `ListIterator` (this line, which is on the index-build path), `ReadResource` and `WriteEvent` in this file still use `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`. `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` in bleve.go does the same. The child DB and `listLatest` work in those functions therefore attaches to the caller's span rather than the new span, and the spans are not nested as intended.

findings.title: Data race on shared err and totalBatchesIndexed in the parallel init workers
findings.body: Inside `group.Go`, each worker does `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...)`. Both variables are shared across goroutines without synchronization, and `err` is the outer variable also used by `GetResourceStats` and `Wait`. This is a data race under `-race`. A worker can also return another worker's `err`, so a failed build can be masked as nil. The `namespaced_indexed` span attribute can be wrong too. With `init` now run at construction time, with potentially many workers, each closure should use a local `err` and an atomic counter.
